chunks: And by this chain, he said,

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: The apostate, his wife is separated from him, and his slaughtered meat is not eaten, and he is asked to repent for three days; if he repents, (he lives), otherwise he is killed on the fourth day.

key_terms.يُسْتَتَابُ: He is asked to repent / given time to repent

ai.seo_question: What are the legal rulings regarding the wife, meat, and execution timeline for an apostate in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) outlines the legal rulings (hukm) regarding an apostate (murtadd) in Shia jurisprudence, specifying that his wife is separated from him, his meat is not considered halal for consumption, and he is given a three-day period to repent before execution on the fourth day if he does not. It highlights the distinction between the civil penalty of separation and the ritual impurity of the apostate, reflecting the early Imami understanding of the 'three-day grace period' (istitabah) as a standard procedural safeguard before capital punishment.

en.hubeali: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(As for the) apostate, his wife should isolate herself from him, and she should not eat meat slaughtered by him, and he would be given three days to repent, so if he does repent (fine), or else he would be killed on the fourth day’.
